sources.entry: Extream Download Manager - a powerful tool to increase download speeds up to 500%

summary.one_liner: Xtreme Download Manager (XDM) is a Java/Swing download manager that splits downloads across multiple connections, resumes interrupted transfers, and grabs videos (HLS/DASH) from streaming sites, with a browser extension for hand-off.
summary.what_it_does: XDM speeds up HTTP downloads by splitting them across multiple connections and can resume downloads interrupted by network drops, crashes or power loss. Its video grabber detects HLS (.m3u8) and MPEG-DASH (.mpd) streams and muxes them to MP4 without external tools, and can save subtitles as .srt. A companion browser extension (Chrome, Firefox and other Chromium/Firefox browsers) forwards downloads and detected media to the running app over a local-only connection on 127.0.0.1:8597. Other features listed include batch "download all links on a page" with filters, social media profile bulk downloads, a scheduler and queues, clipboard paste of links, HTTP/SOCKS proxy and auth support, NTLM authentication, checksum verification, and an optional antivirus scan. A headless command-line mode (xdm-app --headless) is described in the README for HTTP, HLS and DASH downloads. The README states the app is being rebuilt as XDM 9 and is in active development.
use_cases: bulk download all PDFs or images on a web page
download HLS or DASH streams to MP4
command-line downloads on a server or terminal
notable: Multi-connection segmented downloading with resume support
Video grabber for HLS (.m3u8) and MPEG-DASH (.mpd) streams, muxed to MP4 without ffmpeg
Browser extension hands off downloads and detected videos to the app over localhost
Download engine xdm-core is Apache 2.0 licensed and reusable; the app is GPL v3
Headless command-line mode with quality selection
caveats: README says the code is being rewritten and is in active development; contributors are asked to hold off on code pull requests
Building from source requires JDK 25 and Maven
Uninstall and data-folder paths are documented per platform (Windows, macOS, Linux), but the README does not list the full set of supported platforms beyond those named
summary.license: GPL-3.0 (desktop app and browser extensions); xdm-core under Apache-2.0
